samples.summary: Canonical subsystem doc left contradicting the change: template-gallery.md's "Seeding a deployment's gallery" section still states "publishing is JWT-only and the CLI has no `templates` namespace", and builds the rationale for the `seed:templates` / `register:templates` operator split on that premise. This branch adds exactly that namespace (including `publish`) and only updates docs/design/cli.md, so the gallery doc — the design doc the new code itself cites in its header comments — now reads false to the next reader. The repo files docs by validity and expects the canonical subsystem doc to be folded forward rather than left stale beside a second account in cli.md. Cost stays inside the codebase (behaviour is unaffected), hence minor.
samples.evidence: template-gallery.md:983 — "A new deployment's gallery is empty, and there is no way to fill it from outside a browser: publishing is JWT-only and the CLI has no `templates` namespace."

samples.summary: `templates.list`'s declared response omits card fields the server actually returns — `thumbnailId`, `author`, `canManage`, and `review` are all on `TemplateCardView` (packages/backend/src/template/template.service.ts:145-213, `Omit<TemplateListingView,'previewToken'|'documentId'>`), but the schema entry names only id/documentType/title/description/category/tags/visibility/status/useCount/publishedAt. The branch's own lessons note argues the schema must describe a card faithfully so an agent does not script a field that is not there; the inverse gap (a field that is there and undocumented) leaves `wafflebase schema` an incomplete contract for the one consumer it exists for. Same applies to `templates.publish`, whose response entry names six of the fourteen `TemplateListingView` fields.
samples.evidence: registry.ts:1429 response literal vs TemplateCardView in packages/backend/src/template/template.service.ts:210

samples.summary: The namespace is one-way: `templates publish` can widen a document's audience (it mints a non-expiring anonymous `viewer` share link per the gallery design) but there is no `templates unpublish` (`DELETE /templates/:id`, already implemented in TemplateController:82) to revoke it. Every other access-granting CLI verb pairs with a revoke (`api-keys create` / `api-keys revoke`). The task file scopes `DELETE`/`PATCH` out explicitly, so this is a deliberate gap rather than an oversight — but an agent that publishes from a terminal has to open a browser to undo it, which is worth weighing before the namespace ships.
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/template/template.controller.ts:82 `@Delete('templates/:id')` exists and is unused by the CLI; docs/tasks/active/20260914-cli-templates-command-todo.md:38-42 declares it out of scope

samples.summary: `templates use` exposes no `--folder`, though `UseTemplateDto` accepts `folderId` (packages/backend/src/template/template.dto.ts:287) and the CLI already has a `folders` namespace. Every copy therefore lands at the destination workspace root, so a scripted "use this template into my Q1 folder" needs a follow-up `docs move`. Not required by the issue; noted as an available capability left unwired.
